source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Close the hospital immediately without first defining cases or possible exposures","B":"Wait for more infections before collecting data or implementing control measures","C":"Assume the cluster is coincidental unless every affected patient has the same organism","D":"Define and identify cases, analyze exposures, and implement targeted controls"}}
source_row.rationale: A systematic outbreak investigation involves identifying and characterizing cases, analyzing common exposures, timing, or risk factors to identify a likely source or transmission route, and implementing targeted control measures based on these findings, an epidemiological approach used by infection prevention teams to control and prevent further spread.
source_row.source_detail: HAI outbreak investigation: establish case definition, identify/count cases, analyze exposures, implement control measures; accessed 2026-08-14.
source_row.source_name: CDC — Field Epidemiology Manual: Healthcare Settings
source_row.stem: A hospital's infection prevention team investigates a cluster of similar infections occurring on one unit, and a staff member assumes this cluster is probably just a coincidence not worth digging into further. Which step is instead a core component of this outbreak investigation?
